title: Joint residues of the largest prime factors of n and n+1
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: Let P(n) be the largest prime factor of n. Show that the last digits of P(n) and P(n+1) behave like two independent fair choices from {1,3,7,9}: each of the 16 pairs occurs for asymptotically 1/16 of all n. More generally, for any modulus q, the pair (P(n) mod q, P(n+1) mod q) should be uniform over pairs of reduced residues.
math: Let P(n) denote the largest prime factor of n >= 2. Prove that for every q >= 2 and a,b in (Z/qZ)^x, the natural density of {n >= 2: P(n) = a, P(n+1) = b (mod q)} equals phi(q)^{-2}. In particular (q=10), for all a,b in {1,3,7,9}, #{2<=n<=x: P(n)=a, P(n+1)=b (mod 10)} ~ x/16. (A logarithmic-density version is a natural first step.)
